decision: Stop support-only radius expansion and co-design axis spectral notches, dictionary geometry, and patch constraints.
why: Every sampled joint radius through R=16 has at least one reconstructed safe dual block.
A coarse R=16 axis grid produced a reproducible false escape.
The prime-power cutoff grows as exp(2R) and reaches 78,962,960,182,680 at R=16.
first_actions: Extract active axis support locations and weights from every saved witness.
Cluster recurrent peaks by band and radius.
Add controllable value or derivative notch constraints at recurrent peaks.
Rebuild constrained coordinates without increasing support.
Audit each candidate with adaptive axis maximization before accepting alpha below 1.

success_gate.dual: At least one currently blocked patch has no reconstructed safe dual lower bound at or above 1 under refined/adaptive axis audit.
success_gate.primal: A PSD Gram candidate has dense core maximum at most -1 and dense axis-plus-tail objective below 1.

stop_rules: Stop a notch family if energy merely moves to adjacent bands or band edges.
Stop if core negativity is lost faster than axis charge decreases.
Do not expand beyond R=16 before a current-radius dictionary passes the dual gate.
Do not build large arithmetic matrices before a primal candidate survives dense geometric audits.
forbidden_inferences: An alpha below 1 from a searched witness family proves primal feasibility.
A histogram without interval interpolation error is an arithmetic certificate.
A finite-model obstruction proves or disproves RH.
